evidence.text: The account treats 米 as depicting grains, and describes the original sense as grains with their husks removed, including grains from several crops rather than rice alone. It reports oracle-bone uses for rice/grain, for the word 敉 ‘pacify’, and as a sacrificial name; bronze inscriptions often use the graph as a clan name. These are reports in the database, not independently dated lexical attestations in this response.

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析 / graphic analysis
evidence.text: The account says oracle-bone and bronze forms have three small marks above and below a central stroke. It attributes the proposal that the central stroke depicts a sieve (籭) to Li Xiaoding, and records Bai Yuzheng's alternative that it depicts a rice or grain stalk. The identity of the central stroke is therefore disputed; the overall grain pictograph analysis does not depend on resolving it.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：米

evidence.source: NTNU Chinese Academic Annual, article on Wang Yu's Shuowen commentary
evidence.text: The article cites oracle-bone forms (Heji 71 and 32541) and Chu manuscript forms (Xin 2.029 and Bao 2.95). It reports that the dots were joined into strokes before the small-seal form, noting that the Chu forms show the change predates small seal. It reviews differing interpretations: Li Xiaoding's central sieve proposal, Cai Xinfa's scattered-grains pictograph, and Xu Jinxiong's interpretation as shelled grain kernels rather than a particular crop. The article concludes that 米 originally referred broadly to dehusked grain, not one specific grain, and that modern usage often specializes it to rice. It also cautions against a proposed reconstructed preform based only on writing convenience.
evidence.title: 中國學術年刊第四十七期（春季號）

evidence.source: NTNU Chinese Academic Annual, article on Wang Yu's Shuowen commentary
